March, 1991      Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Mr. D.B. Strong, NORTHWICH

Dear Sirs,

Like me, my equipment is a bit
long in the tooth (but I am
rather a newcomer to computing)
and consists of a Spectrum 48K
with Saga Elite 3 keyboard,
Interface 1, single Microdrive
and an Okimate 20 printer.

Normally I only require to use
Word Processor, Bank Account and
Address Book programs but occas-
ionally need to draw diagrams
(using Plot & Draw) curves,
graphs etc. These will print out
hard copy on the ZX Printer with
"COPY" but will not,of course,do
so to a DM Printer.

I am informed that a Screen Dump
program is required.  Would
'CHARCOL',in Outlet Issue 08 (A)
do this or could you recommend
another?

        Yours faithfully,

           D.B. Strong

To:D.B. Strong from Brian Cavers


CHARCOL uses dot-patterns to
represent colours and is very
slow so is not suitable to draw
line drawings, curves etc.It may
be useful for shaded graphs etc.
if time is not important.

No, I would recommend HANDYDUMP
in OUTLET 27 for a good Spectrum
standard-quality screen dump to
a printer.

Incidentally, the next letter by
Ken Stearn and my reply may also
be of interest.

                        - Brian

From Ken Stearn, FIFE

After many years of steady use I
finally moved up from my faith-
ful BROTHER HR5 printer. I have
a new Toshiba Express Writer 301
which I use with my original
Kempston Centronics E Interface
and a 128K +2 (grey) with I'face
1 driving microdrives.The manual
that comes with the Toshiba is
excellent. However,I'm at a loss
understanding how to get the
graphic codes to work. I can get
a copy with the standard Epson
copy but feel sure the machine
is capable of much better. I use
a line like LPRINT CHR$ 27; CHR$
42; CHR$ 1. My problem is what
to enter for the next two bytes:
n1 and n2?          - Ken Stearn

To Ken Stearn from Brian


The last two bytes are the total
number of bytes of image data to
follow in the form: N1 + N2*256.
So, for example, to send 300
bytes of image data,the last two
bytes would be 44 and 1 (= 44 +
256*1 = 300). The reason is that
any bytes (numbers in range 0 to
255) sent to a printer normally
act as special codes, e.g., 65
prints a capital "A", 10 does a
line feed etc. Therefore,sending
to the printer for example...
CHR$ 27; CHR$ 42; CHR$ 1; CHR$
44; CHR$ 1 tells the printer not
to treat the following 300 bytes
as ordinary codes but as image
data.

Now, each byte is made up of 8
bits which are represented as
dots on the screen or print-out.
These are the dots that make up
a screen picture or even the
design of a single character.So,
if there are 8 dots in each byte
then 300 bytes of data would be
2400 "dots". It is clear there
are more than 2400 dots on a
Spectrum screen. How many are
there? The answer is 256 across
by 192 high = 49152. Every byte
can hold 8 dots so divide 49152
and you get 6144 bytes to send
to the printer altogether.

However, it's not that simple!
You can't just tell the printer
to expect 6144 bytes of image
data as they are not in order!

Furthermore, printers will only
accept a limited number in one
"gulp"! Your printer manual will
tell you that, in your chosen
example, there are 960 dots on
each line; this is the most you
can send in one go. However, the
Spectrum screen is only 256 dots
wide so you're well within that.

As mentioned, each byte sent to
the printer consists of 4 bits
or "dots"but the printer regards
these dots VERTICALLY one above
the other in a line. If you sent
a single byte (I'll use binary
numbers here so it's easier to
see the dots) of BIN 10101010, a
vertical line of dot,space, dot,
space etc. would be printed by
the printer.

If you want to try this do...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 42;CHR$ 1;
CHR$ 1; CHR$ 0;CHR$ BIN 10101010

In that example, the N1 and N2
from your query are CHR$ 1 and
CHR$ 0 which tells the printer
to accept ONE byte of image data
(1 + 256 *0 = 1). This is then
followed by the actual byte of
image data, in my example CHR$
BIN 10101010. If you are not
familiar with binary don't worry
as you only need to know it is
just another way of representing
a number. BIN 10101010 is the
same as 170 and you could use
CHR$ 170 instead in the LPRINT.
You can find the value of any
binary number by entering,e.g.,
PRINT BIN 10101010.

Now, how do you calculate what
dots are on the screen and in
what order to send them?In BASIC
you could use the POINT function
which detects which dots are INK
(1) and which PAPER (0) in a FOR
NEXT loop. However, I must warn
you that it will be relatively
slow but is very flexible if you
want to experiment. Write again
if you want details of such a
BASIC routine.

More commonly, machine code is
used to copy the screen to a
printer but it uses the same
principles of calculating the
dots on the screen, converting
8 vertical dots into a byte and
sending them in sequence after
first sending the 27, 42, 1,etc.

HANDYDUMP in OUTLET 27 is such a
machine code routine but is for
single density and will not give
you any better quality than you
already get. When you say "I can
get a copy with the standard
Epson copy" I assume you mean as
provided by the BASIC command
COPY which tells your Kempston E
to use its own, built-in machine
code program to copy the screen.


Incidentally, I was astounded at
the quality of the picture copy
done on your HR5 - the blackness
was perfect - not a streak and
black as jet! You'll be hard
pressed to improve on that with
your average 9-pin dot-matrix
printer!

I'll make a note to have a go at
a new routine for OUTLET which
will concentrate solely on doing
the densest, darkest COPY using
quadruple density. There have
been other routines on the mark-
et such as DUMPY by Bradway
Software.The last address I have
for them is "Hillsett", Upper
Padley, Grindleford, Sheffield,
S30 1JA (Tel: 0433 30799). I
don't if they're still trading.

Incidentally, if you do experi-
ment with a BASIC routine you
must also remember to set the
line spacing so each horizontal
line of 8 vertical dots starts
immediately below the one above
or else you will get a venetian
blind effect!
                        - Brian

From: Mr.C.J. Mockridge,SOMERSET



Dear Ron Cavers,

I have some questions:

 1) What is a microdrive?

 2) What are tracks 40 to 80?

 3) What is Public Domain?


        Yours sincerely,

         C.J. Mockridge


Brian Cavers to C.J. Mockridge


A microdrive is a device used to
store programs and data like a
tape cassette or a +3 drive. It
was produced by Sinclair in the
early Spectrum days and is still
used by many of us. It uses tiny
cartridges containing a loop of
magnetic recording tape on which
to store the programs. It needs
an Interface 1 to connect it to
a Spectrum.

Tracks 40 and 80 are standard
numbers of tracks on a disc.Some
disc drives can only use one
side of the disc, i.e. 40 tracks
and are referred to as single-
sided or 40-track drives.

On our order form, the reference
to 40 and 80 tracks is only in
connection with the Disciple or
+D drives. The +3 uses standard
3" discs with 40 tracks on each
side.

The term, "Public domain" refers
to software (programs) which the
author has stated can be copied
and given away to other people,
so long as no charge, or only a
nominal charge to cover costs,is
made. The author retains the
copyright. Many claim no changes
may be made to such software. In
OUTLET we use the term FREEWARE
for any such programs because we
feel users should be completely
free to make changes, customise,
modify, etc.            - Brian

From: Mr. Chris Ingram, MILAWI

Dear Ron and Brian,

Thank you for continuing to
supply such a variety of soft-
ware in each month's Outlet. I
have a few queries I would
appreciate help with.

The school where I now teach has
a Sinclair 128K Machine(my first
acquaintance with this variety
of Spectrum).Unfortunately, it
has a fault: column 31 of the
screen display appears to the
left of column 0; this applies
right down the screen, to
displays, listings and editing.
Is there a quick way to cure
this or does it need a computer
doctor?

I found the Patience game which
you published as 'Oerkenvan'
(Outlet 23) in a book in the
school library.

In this version you are allowed
one chance after becoming stuck.
All cards not placed in their
correct sequence are picked up,
reshuffled and dealt to the
right of those already placed,
leaving a gap of one card. Play
then continues as before.

The extra go would make the game
a lot more interesting. (I have
spent many hours relaxing with
the published version only to
be defeated each time).

Is there any chance that one of
your programming wizards, or

even the original author, could
adapt the program to include
this option?

In a reply to Bryson Hall in
Outlet 40 you gave P.V.Tubes as
a suitable source of replacement
Spectrum membranes but only gave
the phone number. At about `2 a
minute for international calls
it isn't feasible to chance it,
especially with those not used
to overseas business. Can you
supply their address and perhaps
make a note to do this in future
for the benefit of those of us
not able or willing to phone.

     Keep up the Good Work!

  Yours sincerely, Chris Ingram

Brian Cavers to Chris Ingram

It certainly sounds as if your
Spectrum is faulty.Are there any
repair companies in Malawi? If
not you could try VSE (see our
OUTBOARD).

This problem with OERKENVAN has
come up before. It arose because
the original needed extensive
re-writing but was all in Dutch
(I think!) and so I didn't even
know the rules. By the time I
found out you should be able to
get another chance I couldn't
find out how to do it easily. I
regret it now could involve
several days work to investigate
and re-write it. If anyone would
like to volunteer...

P.V. TUBES are at 104 Abbey St.,
Accrington, Lancs. BB5 1EE.

I will try to remember to always
put a full address in future!

                        - Brian

From: Mr. John Couch.

Dear Both,
I wrote to Dublin for details of
the Cliveprint gear but got no
reply!. So, I took your advice
and bought a Citizen 120D+.
Shock, horror! It would COPY but
not LPRINT or LList!

The answer:
POKE 23354,62:POKE 2355,16.
All was then O.K. but when I
print a page from OUTLET, K
copies the whole page including
the menu.

LPRINT III reports END OF FILE
1420.1.  Any solution would be
gratefully received.

       Regards, John Couch

To John Couch from Brian Cavers


Sorry, but there are so many
different bits of kit we just
cannot cater for all of them. I
need to know what method you are
using to print from OUTLET. Let
me guess. I suspect you have a
Spectrum +2A, the one in a black
case. I suspect you are trying
to print via the printer port of
the Spectrum itself.. I suspect
that the initialization routine
for the +2A is the same as for
the +3...


If all my suspicions are correct
then do the mod on the following
page...

1. Load OUTLET and load the text
article(OUTLETTERS or whatever).

2. Press BREAK

3. Enter...

   1440 FORMAT LPRINT "U"

4. Enter GO TO 1080 to restart
   the program and use the
   Kempston E option.

5. Write to me saying how great
   and amazingly wonderful I am
   or...

6. Write to me saying what an
   absolute waste of time and I
   ought to be locked up or even
   be thrashed with a big stick.

However, if it does work (it'll
be a ruddy miracle) you could
try resaving the program with
RUN 9983 (I assume you are using
the tape version?). I regret it
would be difficult to include an
extra printer option permanently
in OUTLET.

                        - Brian

From:M. Gent, SUTTON-IN-ASHFIELD

Dear Ron & Brian,

I refer to OUTLET 41 printout of
OUTLET text-files and will start
by explaining my set-up.

I have had a Spectrum +2,(grey
case NOT +2A) since 1986 and
last year added a printer and a
disc interface +DD/DD drive.

My printer is a C.ITOH Y10-20
daisywheel with serial cassette
interface, (from EEC). I was
considering a Microdrive from
the same firm but the cost of
cartridges compared with 3.5
in. discs won me over to DATEL
(+D Interface).

I get a good printout of OUTLET
text-files using LPRINT III. The
only problem I had prior to
OUTLET 38 was on single page
printout. The first line of page
2 printed over the last line of
page 1 if I forgot to wind the
paper up a bit before moving
onto the next page. From OUTLET
38 on there is an extra line
feed or two so this does not
happen anymore. The printout
prints a number 7 at the left
margin on the line above the
first text line on page 1. Page
2 on then prints the 7 and then
the text on top of the 7.(1st
char.) The ALL option just
prints the 7 above the text (as
page 1 of page). This,however, I
can live with.

This last month or so have I
used the ALL option. As my
printer does not have a tractor
feed I only used single A4 or A5
paper, like a typewriter. My
local computer shop quoted `18+
for 200 sheets of tractor feed
paper; I decided not to bother.
Instead I bought paper rolls
(4.5 inch wide x 3 inch dia), at
`10 for 3 rolls. I made a wooden
roll holder which is just right
for 32 character printouts.

I have modified my copy of
OUTLET 38's BASIC to store and
print OUTLET textfiles. I put a
custom copy of the contents
BASIC on a disc with the file -
name "CONTENTS.1" followed by 24
text-files, then the BASIC named
"CONTENTS.2" and so on.

As you know there is room for 80
files on a +D disc, so there is
room for quite a few more. The
reason I started this was I had
trouble printing from OUTLET 39,
it crashed on pressing P or A.

This modified program saves me
having to remember to POKE
23349,39:POKE 23350,1 before
loading OUTLET (to pass ESC
codes (chr(27)) via the +2's
RS232 port). I have put these
POKES in line 9900.

I have used lines 12 to 20 for
the modified menu display as
existing lines corrupt when
edited. Line 30 is for prog data
(filenames). The on screen menu
displays prog names and the
keyletters A to T and 1 to 4.

I use No.4 to stop the program.
The menu says 'STOP.PROG...4'.
Pressing 4 stops the program
with 'File not found 300:1'.
This stops the program and also
makes the listing visible.
POKEing 23607,60 does the same
but you cannot see what you are
typing. (However, I was getting
quite good at this.)

I have put all the OUTLET
utilities programs onto two
discs; games etc. on one disc,
and separate discs for outclass,
textfiles,program info.,letters,
drivechat etc. I can now recycle
the monthly OUTLET discs.

On experimenting with DRKODE
assembler I discovered a small
BUG in the SAVE option:-

SAVE DN; N$ CODE etc., is
illegal in G,DOS. SO IS- SAVE
D*; N$ CODE etc. -THE ONLY LEGAL
WAY(see +D instructions) TO SAVE
A VARIABLE NAME IS:- SAVE D1; N$
CODE etc. (or D2)

On SAVEing the textfile the
program CRASHES. It SAVES the
textfile. It's then necessary to
reload DRKODE and the textfile.
On SAVEing the code it CRASHES
again. Modifying the program to
D1 or d1, deleting the input N
prompt (NOT N$ prompt) stops
with '2 VARIABLE NOT FOUND 2:2'
when saving text. Can you
explain this?  I have also
dabbled with JACKSOFT, from
OUTLET EXTRA 1 ). However, they
are both very good assemblers!

I also notice OUTLET 40 did not
contain INDEX DATA. It was in
41, but 41's was not. Is this a
new idea, INDEX DATA for one
issue in the following issue, or
did you forget to put it in?

I would also like to say how
much I enjoy reading OUTLET
every month. I also enjoy the
different software in OUTLET. I
THANK YOU. A bit late I know but
A HAPPY NEW YEAR TO ALL AT
CHEZRON.

        Yours sincerely,

          Malcolm Gent.

To M. Gent from Brian Cavers


Serve you right for skipping the
editorial in a rush to get to
the good bits! In Issue 40's
editorial it does explain that
each month's index data will now
appear the following month.

We tried Dr.Kode on our +D but
could not get it to crash unless
we tried to save an empty file,
that is, to save a listing with
no listing! SAVE DN; N$ and SAVE
D*; N$ is quite legal on the +D.
Can you pinpoint the place in
the manual where it says the
only legal way is SAVE D1? I'm
at a loss to guess what may be
different about your system.

If anyone else can throw any
light on this I'd be interested
as I've spent a lot of time with
no solution in sight! It's hard
to cure a fault when you can't
make the fault happen!

The only vague things that may
be relevant that I can think of
is that you may be in 128K and
there is a line 0. I've an idea
128K may not like line 0's much!
However, it works on our +3. The
other thing is that memory is
EXTREMELY tight. Only about 700
bytes are free.Have you made any
changes to the BASIC which may
limit this even more and cause
problems when the +D operates?

                        - Brian

From: Terry Filby, BECCLES

Thanks for "Outlet" No.036; it's
nice to be back with you after a
few months break.

The reason I wanted this partic-
ular disk was primarily because
of the Bach program. Music is
very important to me both as an
amateur performer and mostly as
a listener. I like all music as
long as it's well performed,
which I am afraid excludes most
"pop" but my favourite type is
classical.

The Spectrum +3 isn't ideally
suited but I'd like to hear from
anyone who has programmed any
classical music, on its own or
as MSC files for "Music Writer".

Is it possible with hardware
modification to make the +3's
sound clearer? Thanks to Chris
for "Bach" and I hope more to
come. Wish I was a programmer!

        Yours sincerely,

           Terry Filby

To Terry Filby from Brian Gaff

The +3 is indeed a mess as far
as sound is concerned. At
present I know of no really
worthwhile mods for it. However,
the +2A has better sound and
Amstrad SAY they made quite a
lot of +3As, yes, I do really
mean that!

These machines also have good
sound. The best sound of all
though, is from the old black
128 and grey +2s. If all you
want to do is replay your code,
it might be worth buying one of
these second hand, and porting
the code over via the RS232.
There are some programs about
able to do this.

If anyone out there has a mod
for the awful sound of the +3,
we would love to see (hear?) it!

                         - B.G.

From: John Lunn, BOLTON.

Dear Ron & Brian,

Thank you for sending me the
"back issues" and your note of
good wishes was appreciated and
shows that you have a genuine
concern for your subscribers and
contributors, which is a very
welcome contrast to another
publication's care and integrity
towards its members. This leads
me into the following points:-

1) Re: The adverse publicity the
"other publication" gets. I can
sympathise with and feel Mike
Jones' frustration as my exper-
ience is identical, "only the
dates and amount can be changed
to condemn the guilty".

2) In contrast, I can endorse
comments of praise and help
towards 'Microsnips, Wallasey'.
No matter how small the request
they are extremely helpful and
courteous.

3) REF. Thermal paper.
Until I upgraded from the serial
8056 to the LC1O I used to get
my thermal paper from Inmac Ltd.
(business and computer office
suppliers). For an 8.5 inch x
300ft (three hundred) roll the
cost was `6.75 + VAT.(Order code
5605-1).However, in their latest
catalogue it seems they deleted
this item,therefore it may still
be worth pursuing as this type
of company nearly always reduce
the price on deleted items left
in stock.

Inmac have branches nationwide.
Try ringing their Runcorn branch
Tel: 0928 712539.

4)RE: Print out from Masterfile.
I use the excellent "Dumpy"
programme from Bradway Software.
This enables you to print out in
various sizes. My method is as
follows:-

A) Configure the Dumpy code to
suit print size and load onto
Masterfile data disk. (I usually
have four sizes.)

B) Load in Masterfile prog. and
data as usual.

C) Alter BASIC as follows (using
L then CAPSHIFT 6)

4010 POKE @6,1=FOR +D
4010 RANDOMIZE USR XXXXX=ADDRESS
YOU WANT DUMPY TO WORK AT
(I USE 61000)
4015 GOTO 4000=TO GET SEQUENCE
OF PRINT
5000 CAT 1=CAT FOR +D
5001 PAUSE 500=ENOUGH TIME TO
READ CAT.

To use:-

A)Load in masterfile and data
B)Select data you require to
display/print
C)Break into BASIC in usual way
or via "U" on main menu and
break
D)Load the Dumpy you require
E)GOTO 100=Brings up main menu
F)PRESS P

Notes:-
Until you want to change the
print-out you can re-select and
print data without going into
BASIC again. After a few crashes
and !*?@!* words, I found it
best to leave approx 1k memory
free in data bank.

Are Campbell planning to convert
the +3 Masterfile which uses the
128K capacity to the +2? It is
needed by many users.

5) A query:Whilst using the Dor-
ling Kindersley Spectrum Prog-
ramming,Book 4 the Sprite editor
page 11 has the following line:-

330 IF s<a-1+21*32 THEN LET
S=S-32: GOTO 140

On typing the full program into
my +2 (grey) and cursing why it
did not work I noticed the line
330 read as follows:-

330 IF sa<-1+21*32 THEN LET
S=S-32: GOTO 140


An error on my part, try again,
the same result (i.e. a<)
transposed.

After attempting in both 128 and
48 mode my +2 would not accept
the correct way. Every time I
pressed enter the transposition
took place.

I attempted this line on two
more +2's same result.

On typing the line into my son's
old 128+ the line was accepted.
I then saved this line, merged
by tape into +2 and it was
accepted.

Can you give an indication as to
why this phenomenon took place?

6) REF: Solitaire in Issue 39.
This took me back to my child-
hood as I was given the "wooden
board and marbles" version by
by grandfather and, like others
today on the computer, many
frustrating hours were spent in
solving the puzzle. Since this
discovery and especially as an
adult,I have "won a number of
free pints" when this game has
been produced.

A hint for those who have yet to
solve the puzzle: concentrate on
one side at a time. There I've
gone and reduced the potential
number of free pints!

          Kind regards,

            John Lunn

To John Lunn from Brian Gaff

Thanks for all the info on
Masterfile, etc. I am sure many
users will find it useful. I can
certainly recommend DUMPY as I
use it for printing out Prestel
frames through the +3 Centronics
port. It can configure screen
dumps for almost every use.

I see you have fallen foul of
the mysterious 128K editor bug!
My 128K has a +2 ROM, so I do
not know if it afflicts the
earlier black model. The way
around the problem is simple,
just add a space AFTER the '<'
symbol. You do not need such a
complex line to cause the
problem, either. Try this...

10 IF c>d1 THEN GO TO 10

This becomes...

10 IF cd>1 THEN GO TO 10

        ...which is not terribly
helpful! Adding a space is the
answer though.

                           B.G.

Does anyone know how to disable
the verify in the Disciple's
FORMAT routine?

                       - Brian.

From: Mr. D.B. Strong, NORTHWICH

Dear Sirs,

Like me, my equipment is a bit long in the tooth (but I am rather a newcomer to computing) and consists of a Spectrum 48K with Saga Elite 3 keyboard, Interface 1, single Microdrive and an Okimate 20 printer.

Normally I only require to use Word Processor, Bank Account and Address Book programs but occas- ionally need to draw diagrams (using Plot & Draw) curves, graphs etc. These will print out hard copy on the ZX Printer with "COPY" but will not,of course,do so to a DM Printer.

I am informed that a Screen Dump program is required.  Would 'CHARCOL',in Outlet Issue 08 (A) do this or could you recommend another?

Yours faithfully,

D.B. Strong

From Ken Stearn, FIFE

After many years of steady use I finally moved up from my faith- ful BROTHER HR5 printer. I have a new Toshiba Express Writer 301 which I use with my original Kempston Centronics E Interface and a 128K +2 (grey) with I'face 1 driving microdrives.The manual that comes with the Toshiba is excellent. I use a line like LPRINT CHR$ 27; CHR$ 42; CHR$ 1. My problem is what to enter for the next two bytes: n1 and n2?          - Ken Stearn

To Ken Stearn from Brian

The last two bytes are the total number of bytes of image data to follow in the form: N1 + N2*256. So, for example, to send 300 bytes of image data,the last two bytes would be 44 and 1 (= 44 + 256*1 = 300). The reason is that any bytes (numbers in range 0 to 255) sent to a printer normally act as special codes, e.g., 65 prints a capital "A", 10 does a line feed etc. Therefore,sending to the printer for example... CHR$ 27; CHR$ 42; CHR$ 1; CHR$ 44; CHR$ 1 tells the printer not to treat the following 300 bytes as ordinary codes but as image data.

Now, each byte is made up of 8 bits which are represented as dots on the screen or print-out. These are the dots that make up a screen picture or even the design of a single character.So, if there are 8 dots in each byte then 300 bytes of data would be 2400 "dots". It is clear there are more than 2400 dots on a Spectrum screen. How many are there? The answer is 256 across by 192 high = 49152. Every byte can hold 8 dots so divide 49152 and you get 6144 bytes to send to the printer altogether.

However, it's not that simple! You can't just tell the printer to expect 6144 bytes of image data as they are not in order!

Furthermore, printers will only accept a limited number in one "gulp"! Your printer manual will tell you that, in your chosen example, there are 960 dots on each line; this is the most you can send in one go. However, the Spectrum screen is only 256 dots wide so you're well within that.

As mentioned, each byte sent to the printer consists of 4 bits or "dots"but the printer regards these dots VERTICALLY one above the other in a line. If you sent a single byte (I'll use binary numbers here so it's easier to see the dots) of BIN 10101010, a vertical line of dot,space, dot, space etc. would be printed by the printer.

If you want to try this do...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 42;CHR$ 1; CHR$ 1; CHR$ 0;CHR$ BIN 10101010

In that example, the N1 and N2 from your query are CHR$ 1 and CHR$ 0 which tells the printer to accept ONE byte of image data (1 + 256 *0 = 1). This is then followed by the actual byte of image data, in my example CHR$ BIN 10101010. If you are not familiar with binary don't worry as you only need to know it is just another way of representing a number. BIN 10101010 is the same as 170 and you could use CHR$ 170 instead in the LPRINT. You can find the value of any binary number by entering,e.g., PRINT BIN 10101010.

Now, how do you calculate what dots are on the screen and in what order to send them?In BASIC you could use the POINT function which detects which dots are INK (1) and which PAPER (0) in a FOR NEXT loop. However, I must warn you that it will be relatively slow but is very flexible if you want to experiment. Write again if you want details of such a BASIC routine.

More commonly, machine code is used to copy the screen to a printer but it uses the same principles of calculating the dots on the screen, converting 8 vertical dots into a byte and sending them in sequence after first sending the 27, 42, 1,etc.

HANDYDUMP in OUTLET 27 is such a machine code routine but is for single density and will not give you any better quality than you already get. When you say "I can get a copy with the standard Epson copy" I assume you mean as provided by the BASIC command COPY which tells your Kempston E to use its own, built-in machine code program to copy the screen.

Incidentally, I was astounded at the quality of the picture copy done on your HR5 - the blackness was perfect - not a streak and black as jet! You'll be hard pressed to improve on that with your average 9-pin dot-matrix printer!

I'll make a note to have a go at a new routine for OUTLET which will concentrate solely on doing the densest, darkest COPY using quadruple density. There have been other routines on the mark- et such as DUMPY by Bradway Software.The last address I have for them is "Hillsett", Upper Padley, Grindleford, Sheffield, S30 1JA (Tel: 0433 30799). I don't if they're still trading.

Incidentally, if you do experi- ment with a BASIC routine you must also remember to set the line spacing so each horizontal line of 8 vertical dots starts immediately below the one above or else you will get a venetian blind effect!

### От: Ken Stearn, FIFE

— Ken Stearn

#### Ответ Ken Stearn от Brian:

Последние два байта представляют собой общее количество байтов данных изображения, которые последуют далее, в виде: N1 + N2*256. Так, например, чтобы отправить 300 байт данных изображения, последними двумя байтами будут 44 и 1 (= 44 + 256*1 = 300). Причина в том, что любые байты (числа в диапазоне от 0 до 255), отправляемые на принтер, обычно действуют как специальные коды, например, 65 печатает заглавную букву «A», 10 выполняет перевод строки и т. д. Поэтому отправка на принтер, к примеру...

`CHR$ 27; CHR$ 42; CHR$ 1; CHR$ 44; CHR$ 1`

сообщает принтеру, что следующие 300 байтов следует рассматривать не как обычные коды, а как данные изображения.

Каждый байт состоит из 8 битов, которые отображаются в виде точек на экране или на распечатке. Это те самые точки, из которых состоит изображение на экране или даже рисунок отдельного символа. Итак, если в каждом байте содержится 8 точек, то 300 байтов данных составят 2400 «точек». Понятно, что на экране Spectrum гораздо больше 2400 точек. Сколько же их там? Ответ: 256 по горизонтали на 192 по вертикали = 49152. Каждый байт может содержать 8 точек, поэтому делим 49152 на 8 и получаем всего 6144 байта, которые нужно отправить на принтер.

Однако не все так просто! Вы не можете просто сказать принтеру ожидать 6144 байта графических данных, поскольку они расположены не по порядку!

Кроме того, принтеры принимают за один «присест» лишь ограниченное количество данных! Руководство к вашему принтеру подскажет вам, что в выбранном вами примере на каждой строке приходится 960 точек; это максимум, который вы можете отправить за один раз. Впрочем, ширина экрана Spectrum составляет всего 256 точек, так что вы с запасом укладываетесь в этот лимит.

Как уже упоминалось, каждый отправляемый на принтер байт состоит из 8 бит (точек), но принтер воспринимает эти точки ВЕРТИКАЛЬНО — одна над другой в столбик. Если вы отправите один байт (я буду использовать здесь двоичные числа, чтобы точки были нагляднее) вида `BIN 10101010`, принтер напечатает вертикальную линию: точка, пробел, точка, пробел и т. д.

Если хотите попробовать, выполните:

```text
LPRINT CHR$ 27; CHR$ 42; CHR$ 1; CHR$ 1; CHR$ 0; CHR$ BIN 10101010
```

В этом примере N1 и N2 из вашего вопроса — это `CHR$ 1` и `CHR$ 0`, что сообщает принтеру о необходимости принять ОДИН байт графических данных (1 + 256 * 0 = 1). За этим следует сам байт данных изображения, в моем примере — `CHR$ BIN 10101010`. Если вы не знакомы с двоичной системой счисления, не волнуйтесь: вам нужно лишь знать, что это просто другой способ представления числа. `BIN 10101010` — это то же самое, что и 170, и вы могли бы вместо этого использовать в LPRINT `CHR$ 170`. Значение любого двоичного числа можно узнать, введя, например, `PRINT BIN 10101010`.

Теперь о том, как рассчитать, какие точки находятся на экране и в каком порядке их отправлять? В BASIC вы можете использовать функцию `POINT`, которая в цикле `FOR...NEXT` определяет, какие точки относятся к INK (1), а какие — к PAPER (0). Однако должен предупредить, что это будет работать относительно медленно, хотя и дает большую гибкость для экспериментов. Напишите еще раз, если вам понадобятся подробности о такой подпрограмме на BASIC.

Чаще для копирования экрана на принтер используется машинный код, но в нем заложены те же принципы: вычисление точек на экране, преобразование 8 вертикальных точек в байт и отправка их по порядку после предварительной передачи кодов 27, 42, 1 и т. д.

#### Brian Cavers отвечает C.J. Mockridge:

Microdrive — это устройство для хранения программ и данных, подобное магнитофонной кассете или дисководу +3. Оно выпускалось компанией Sinclair на заре существования Spectrum и до сих пор используется многими из нас. В нем применяются крошечные картриджи с кольцом магнитной ленты, на которую записываются программы. Для подключения к Spectrum требуется Interface 1.

40 и 80 дорожек — это стандартное количество дорожек на диске. Некоторые дисководы могут использовать только одну сторону диска, то есть 40 дорожек, и называются односторонними, или 40-дорожечными накопителями.

В нашем бланке заказа упоминание 40 и 80 дорожек относится исключительно к дисководам Disciple или +D. Компьютер +3 использует стандартные 3-дюймовые диски с 40 дорожками на каждой стороне.

Термин «Public domain» (общественное достояние) относится к программному обеспечению, в отношении которого автор заявил, что его можно копировать и передавать другим людям при условии, что за это не взимается плата (или берется лишь номинальная сумма для покрытия расходов). При этом автор сохраняет за собой авторские права. Многие заявляют, что в такие программы нельзя вносить изменения. В OUTLET мы используем термин FREEWARE для любых подобных программ, поскольку считаем, что пользователи должны иметь полную свободу вносить изменения, настраивать под себя, модифицировать и т. д.

— Brian

4. КАСАТЕЛЬНО распечатки из Masterfile.  
Я использую отличную программу «Dumpy» от Bradway Software. Она позволяет делать распечатки в различных размерах. Мой метод заключается в следующем:

A) Сконфигурируйте код Dumpy под нужный размер печати и сохраните на диск с данными Masterfile. (Обычно у меня заготовлено четыре размера.)

B) Загрузите программу Masterfile и данные как обычно.

C) Измените BASIC следующим образом (используя `L`, затем `CAPS SHIFT` + `6`):

```text
4010 POKE @6,1: REM ДЛЯ +D
4010 RANDOMIZE USR XXXXX: REM АДРЕС, ГДЕ ДОЛЖЕН РАБОТАТЬ DUMPY (Я ИСПОЛЬЗУЮ 61000)
4015 GOTO 4000: REM ЧТОБЫ ПОЛУЧИТЬ ПОСЛЕДОВАТЕЛЬНОСТЬ ПЕЧАТИ
5000 CAT 1: REM КАТАЛОГ ДЛЯ +D
5001 PAUSE 500: REM ДОСТАТОЧНО ВРЕМЕНИ, ЧТОБЫ ПРОЧИТАТЬ КАТАЛОГ
```

Порядок использования:

A) Загрузите Masterfile и данные.  
B) Выберите данные, которые вы хотите просмотреть/напечатать.  
C) Выйдите в BASIC обычным способом или через пункт меню «U» и Break.  
D) Загрузите нужную версию Dumpy.  
E) `GOTO 100` — возврат в главное меню.  
F) Нажмите `P`.

Примечания:  
Пока вы не захотите изменить формат распечатки, можно повторно выбирать и печатать данные без повторного выхода в BASIC. После пары вылетов и кучи отборных ругательств я выяснил, что в банке данных лучше оставлять свободными около 1 Кб памяти.
